chunk_findings.detail: The `._targets` import block omits `writes_config`, even though the manifest says `ddflow/services/adopt/_targets.py` defines/adds `writes_config`. Because this change advertises the package `__init__` as re-exporting the old `ddflow.services.adopt` public API unchanged, any existing caller using `from ddflow.services.adopt import writes_config` or `ddflow.services.adopt.writes_config` now gets `ImportError`/`AttributeError`. The omission is also reflected in `__all__`, so `from ddflow.services.adopt import *` will not expose it either.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/__init__.py:132

chunk_findings.detail: The public `force` parameter is accepted but never used or forwarded anywhere in the function. A call such as `adopt(repo, ["claude"], force=True)` follows exactly the same path as `force=False`: `_backup_docs` is invoked with a literal `None` instead of the caller’s force flag, and no other call (`init_files`, `_write_driver`, `_upsert_block`, `E.install`, etc.) receives `force`. Thus callers relying on `force=True` to overwrite existing docs/sections or bypass backup/overwrite checks silently get the non-forced behavior, contradicting the stated public API/no-behavior-change intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_adopt.py:24 (adopt)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard is documented as checking whether `AGENTS.md` is listed under `read:`, but the block alternative matches any line that is just `AGENTS.md` or `- AGENTS.md`, and the inline alternative matches bracketed `AGENTS.md` in trailing comments or filenames like `AGENTS.md.bak` because `.` is a word boundary. For `.aider.conf.yml` containing `read: # [AGENTS.md]` (a null `read:` with only a comment), or `read: []` followed by another key such as `watch-files:\n  - AGENTS.md`, `_aider_lists_agents_md()` returns True and `_add_aider_read()` returns “already loads” without ever adding a real `read:` entry, so Aider is not wired up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:_AIDER_LISTED

chunk_findings.detail:
For the valid YAML form
```yaml
read:
- CONVENTIONS.md
```
the block-entry loop uses `re.match(r"^\s+-\s*(.+?)\s*$", line)`, which requires leading whitespace, so it consumes none of the zero-indented sequence entries. The replacement becomes
```yaml
read:
  - AGENTS.md
- CONVENTIONS.md
```
which is not a valid mapping with a single `read:` sequence; the operator’s entry is left at root indentation and the config can fail to parse.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:_add_aider_read

chunk_findings.detail: This function treats any `#` in a scalar as a comment, but YAML comments require preceding whitespace. Given valid `read: file#1.md`, `_aider_read_values()` returns `(['file'], ' #1.md')`, so `_add_aider_read()` writes `read: #1.md` plus a `file` entry, silently dropping the `#1.md` path component. For `read: "file#1.md"`, it can emit an unclosed quoted scalar such as `  - "file`, corrupting the file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:_aider_read_values

chunk_findings.detail: The inline-list parser splits on commas without quote awareness. Given valid YAML `read: ["docs,style.md"]`, the inner value is split into `"docs` and `style.md"`, then stripped to `docs` and `style.md`; `_add_aider_read()` replaces the original single path with two bogus read entries and loses the intended comma-containing filename.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:_aider_read_values

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard fails to recognise a block list item with a trailing comment. Given
```yaml
read:
  - AGENTS.md # instructions
```
`_aider_lists_agents_md()` returns False because the regex requires end-of-line immediately after `AGENTS.md`, so `_add_aider_read()` appends another `  - AGENTS.md` entry, creating a duplicate read entry on the first adopt.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:_AIDER_LISTED

chunk_findings.detail: When an existing command file contains the ddflow marker but the managed region is malformed enough that `region.owns(existing)` raises `RegionError`, this function sets `owned = False` and then falls through to overwrite the file because `MANAGED_MARK` is present in the text. The code comments explicitly say a broken region is the operator’s file and should be left alone, but a file with a `<!-- DDFLOW:MANAGED` begin line and a missing/broken end line or stamp has the marker, so `_write_command` replaces it with the template without backup or a newer-content refusal. Concrete input: `repo/commands/implement.md` contains an operator’s `/implement` workflow plus a ddflow begin marker line but no valid closing region/stamp; `region.owns` raises `RegionError`, `MANAGED_MARK in existing` is true, and adopt overwrites the operator’s file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_commands.py:_write_command

chunk_findings.detail: When `launch="auto"` and ddflow is running from a source checkout, the Docker branch can still be selected: if `uvx` and `ddflow-mcp` are not on `PATH` but `docker` is, the condition `launch == "auto" and not shutil.which("uvx") and not shutil.which("ddflow-mcp") and shutil.which("docker")` is true and `_launch_entry` returns the Docker entry with the default `ghcr.io/OWNER/ddflow:latest` image. That contradicts the function’s own “Source checkout: point at THIS tree” fallback and the `_register_mcp` comment that source checkouts must not configure against a published image. For example, a developer adopting from a source tree with Docker installed but no `uvx` or `ddflow-mcp` on `PATH` gets an MCP config that tries to run the placeholder Docker image instead of `python -m ddflow.surfaces.mcp` from the checkout, so the adopted project does not use the code under test and may fail immediately on an invalid image reference.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_launch.py:_launch_entry

chunk_findings.detail: `has_legacy_block` treats the legacy marker strings as a block whenever they appear anywhere in the file (`LEGACY_BEGIN in text` and `LEGACY_END in text`), and `block_body` slices between their first occurrences. `block_spans` deliberately ignores markers that are not whole line-start lines, so an adopted project whose `AGENTS.md` merely documents the markers, e.g. a line containing `` `<!-- DDFLOW:BEGIN (managed — edits inside this block are overwritten) -->` `` followed later by a line containing `` `<!-- DDFLOW:END -->` ``, has no managed block. `block_spans` returns no span, but `block_body` returns the text between the two prose markers, `has_legacy_block` is true, and `_block_state` returns `STALE`; `rules_status` therefore reports an absent/removed section as stale instead of `NO_BLOCK`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_rules.py:block_body / has_legacy_block

chunk_findings.detail: For a file whose content is exactly `LEGACY_BEGIN + "\n" + project_body(docs_dir) + "\n" + LEGACY_END`, `_block_state` returns `STALE` because the block is legacy and needs migration, even though its body matches the current generated body. The resulting `RulesState` has `stamped=False`, `edited=False`, and `newer=False`, so `_stale_line` renders “`AGENTS.md`'s ddflow section differs from what this ddflow writes …” even though the body does not differ; only the marker grammar is old.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_rules.py:RulesState._stale_line

chunk_findings.detail:
The native-rule binding check searches the entire file with `re.search(r"^alwaysApply:\s*true\s*$", got, re.M)` instead of checking the frontmatter. Given a Cursor rule file such as:
```text
---
alwaysApply: false
---
Example:
alwaysApply: true
```
`got != want_native`, the regex finds the body line, and `rules_status` returns `STALE` rather than `NOT_BINDING`, even though the frontmatter says the rule does not bind and it may never be loaded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_rules.py:rules_status

chunk_findings.detail: The `.ddflow/.gitignore` body ignores `index.db-*` but not the main SQLite database file `index.db`. On a fresh project where ddflow creates `.ddflow/index.db`, the generated `.ddflow/.gitignore` does not match that file, so the `git add .ddflow` step instructed by `init` can commit the derived index. That is precisely the condition the surrounding comment says must be avoided because a committed index can resurrect dead agents' leases; the pattern needs to cover `index.db` itself (e.g. `index.db` and `index.db-*`, or `index.db*`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_scaffold.py:DDFLOW_GITIGNORE

chunk_findings.detail: `local_edits_path` chooses a backup path by checking `candidate.exists()` and then later writing with `atomic_write`, but the check and the write are not atomic. If two `adopt`/`_upsert_block` invocations run concurrently on the same file that has hand edits, both can call `local_edits_path(path)` before either has written the aside. Since `path.name + ".local-edits"` does not yet exist in either process, both return the same aside path. The second `atomic_write(aside, path.read_bytes())` then overwrites the first process’s backup (or, if `atomic_write` is exclusive, raises `FileExistsError`), so the first invocation’s preserved hand edits are lost or the update crashes. The numbering logic is therefore not safe under the interleaving this function’s “numbered when taken” contract implies.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_upsert.py:20 `local_edits_path`

chunk_findings.detail: The lazy `__getattr__` only intercepts attribute lookup on the package object (`getattr(UA, name)`); it does not redirect name resolution inside the submodules. Because the split moves helpers such as `_apply_config`, `_run`, `_abs`, and `_writes_config` into `_appliers` while keeping `apply` and its state in `_apply`, a test or caller that does `monkeypatch.setattr(UA, "_apply_config", fake)` (or similarly patches `_run`, `_LAST`, etc.) changes only `UA._apply_config`. When `UA.apply(...)` runs, the `_apply` module calls its own imported `_apply_config`/`_run` or mutates its own `_LAST`, so the fake is ignored. In the old one-file module these were all globals in the same module as `apply`, so patching `UA._apply_config` did change the call; the docstring’s claim that monkeypatching is preserved “exactly as before” is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/__init__.py:__getattr__

chunk_findings.detail: The package has no `__all__`, so `from ddflow.services.upgrade_apply import *` uses the package’s `__dict__` keys, not `__dir__` or `__getattr__`. Therefore star-import yields only the eagerly bound names (`UP` and the `backups` names) and omits public lazy names such as `apply` and `Watch`, which were in the old module’s globals. This changes the public API/star-import behavior despite the docstring claiming every old exported name is re-exported.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/__init__.py:__dir__

chunk_findings.detail: Given `spec="all,bogus"` (or `spec=["all", "bogus"]`), the function checks `if not names or "all" in names:` before it computes `bad`, so it returns `list(UP.CATEGORIES)` and never raises for `bogus`. This contradicts the documented behavior that an unknown category name raises `ValueError`, and it can silently turn a mistyped filter such as `--categories all,confg` into “apply every category” instead of failing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/_appliers.py:34 (parse_categories)

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor moved the per-item appliers out of `_apply.py` into `._appliers`, but the only names imported from `._appliers` here are `parse_categories` and `touched`. The unchanged apply section below the `# -- the apply --` context line still depends on the moved appliers by bare name (e.g. `_apply_config`, `_apply_hook`, `_apply_mcp`) as it did before the split. Therefore, running `ddflow upgrade --apply` with any plan item in the `config`, `hooks`, or `mcp` category raises `NameError` for the missing applier name instead of applying the item; if a module-level dispatch table was left unchanged, importing `_apply` fails immediately for the same reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/_apply.py:29 (`from ._appliers import parse_categories, touched`)

chunk_findings.detail: The package re-exports the functions, but the moved functions retain the globals of their new submodules, so rebinding names on `ddflow.api.rules` is no longer equivalent to rebinding them on the old single `ddflow/api/rules.py` module. For example, a test or runtime override that does `ddflow.api.rules.DEFAULT_RULE_PRIORITY = 99` (or patches a helper such as `_answer_other_kind`) and then calls `ddflow.api.rules.rule_add(...)` would have affected the function’s global lookup before the split; after this change `rule_add` is `ddflow.api.rules.add.rule_add` and resolves those names in `ddflow.api.rules.add.__dict__`, not in the package `__init__` namespace, so the override is ignored. This is a behavior change introduced by the refactor despite the stated intent of no behavior change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rules/__init__.py:5

chunk_findings.detail: The lazy re-export does not preserve monkeypatching semantics for functions that call each other inside the same submodule. In the old single module, `work` and `_absorb` shared the same module globals, so `monkeypatch.setattr(PR, "_absorb", fake)` changed the global seen by `work`. After the split, `PR.work` returns the function defined in `ddflow.core.progress.tracking`, whose globals are the `tracking` module; `monkeypatch.setattr(PR, "_absorb", fake)` only sets an attribute on the package, not `tracking._absorb`. Thus a test that patches `PR._absorb` (or another private helper such as `PR._duplicate_work` used by `PR.detect`) and then calls the public function through `PR` will still execute the original helper, contrary to the stated “monkeypatch … exactly as before” invariant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/progress/__init__.py:__getattr__

chunk_findings.detail: `from ddflow.core.progress import *` changes behavior because the public names are only lazily available through `__getattr__` and no `__all__` is defined. Python’s star-import uses the module namespace, not `__getattr__`, so it will not bind names such as `work`, `detect`, or `new_reports_line` unless they have already been placed in the package namespace. It will instead bind current public globals such as `importlib` and `Any`. For example, code doing `from ddflow.core.progress import *` and then calling `new_reports_line(...)` would previously work but now fails with `NameError`, violating the “public API unchanged” claim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/progress/__init__.py:__all__ / star import

chunk_findings.detail: The lossy-name matching in `diff_covers_everything` can report a changed path as covered when the matching diff section actually belongs to a different path. The implementation builds `room` from all diff sections whose names equal `lossy(p)` for an absent path, without first reserving sections that already match exact changed paths. Given a repository where two tracked files changed: one file is literally named `a\ufffd`, and another is named with an invalid UTF-8 byte represented in Python as `a\udcff` (so `os.fsencode('a\udcff').decode('utf-8', 'replace')` also yields `a\ufffd`). If the diff produced for the change contains only the section for `a\ufffd`, then `shown` contains `a\ufffd`, `absent` contains `a\udcff`, `room['a\ufffd']` is 1, and the function returns `(True, [])` even though the invalid-byte file is not represented in the diff. This is exactly the silent omission the cross-check is supposed to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:diff_covers_everything

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest states that `_locate.py` defines a top-level `error`, but `_SUBMODULE_OF` has no entry for `"error"`. Because `__getattr__` only lazily imports a submodule for names present in `_SUBMODULE_OF`, `from ddflow.infra.worktree import error` or `W.error(...)` will raise `AttributeError: module 'ddflow.infra.worktree' has no attribute 'error'`, even though the old single-file module had `error` as a top-level attribute. This also means `dir(W)` omits `error`, contradicting the stated unchanged public API.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/__init__.py:_SUBMODULE_OF

chunk_findings.detail: If a worktree directory already exists at the computed `path` and contains `.git`, the function returns immediately without checking or enforcing that the existing checkout is on the requested `branch`. For example, if an earlier run created `.worktrees/item` on branch `task/item`, and a later call uses `create(..., item_id="item", branch="feature/item")`, the early return produces a `Worktree` whose `.branch` field is `"feature/item"` while the actual git `HEAD` in that path is still `task/item`. Subsequent code that trusts `wt.branch` (e.g., merge/push/checked-out-at logic) will operate on the wrong branch or fail with confusing errors.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: `capture_diff` calls `_W.git(tree, "add", "-N", "--", *untracked)` and ignores the result. `_W.git` returns a result object (the same function checks `found.ok` for `merge-base`), so a failing `git add -N` is silently swallowed. For example, in a repository with a valid `HEAD`, one tracked file, one new untracked file, and a stale `.git/index.lock`, `git add -N` fails while `git diff HEAD` can still read the repository and returns an empty diff because there are no tracked changes. The function then returns `""` as if nothing changed, omitting the new file and violating the docstring’s promise that failures are never an empty “nothing changed”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:44 (`capture_diff`)

chunk_findings.detail: The filter `if p.strip()` drops any untracked path whose entire name is whitespace. Given an untracked file whose name is a single space (`" "`), `G.files(tree, "untracked")` returns `[" "]`, but `p.strip()` is empty, so the path is omitted from `untracked_files`. `capture_diff` therefore never runs `git add -N` for that file, and the review diff silently lacks the new file; `diff_covers_everything` would report it as missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:91 (`untracked_files`)

chunk_findings.detail: The lossy-collision accounting can count one diff section twice. `room` is initialized from `seen.count(name)` for absent paths, but `seen` still contains sections that already covered exact changed paths. Suppose two changed paths exist: `bad\udcff` (a filename containing an invalid UTF-8 byte) and `bad\ufffd` (a valid filename containing U+FFFD). If the diff contains only one section for `bad\ufffd`, `shown` already covers the valid path, so only `bad\udcff` is absent. But `lossy(bad\udcff) == bad\ufffd` and `room[bad\ufffd]` is `seen.count("bad\ufffd") == 1`, so the loop decrements it and returns `(True, [])`. The same single diff section is used once as exact coverage and again as lossy coverage, falsely reporting the missing invalid-named file as covered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:119 (`diff_covers_everything`)

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_local_files_report` promises `SKIP_FAILED` and says the copy must not kill the claim, but its cleanup can raise. If a destination parent component exists as a regular file, e.g. `tree/sub` is a file and `names=["sub/file"]`, `dst.exists()` returns false, `dst.parent.mkdir(...)` raises `FileExistsError`/`NotADirectoryError`, and then `dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)` raises `NotADirectoryError` because `missing_ok` only suppresses `FileNotFoundError`. That exception escapes the `except OSError` block instead of returning `SKIP_FAILED`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_local.py:70

chunk_findings.detail: The source is resolved and checked against `root`, but the destination is never canonicalized or checked against `tree`, so the function can copy outside the worktree. For example, with `primary=/repo`, `tree=/repo/wt`, `tree/sub` a symlink to an existing directory `/outside`, primary containing `/repo/sub/file`, and `/outside/file` absent, `src` passes the repository check, `dst` is `/repo/wt/sub/file`, `dst.exists()` and `dst.is_symlink()` are false, `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` succeeds through the symlinked parent, and `shutil.copy2` writes `/outside/file` — outside the tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_local.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: `scratch_tree` promises that nothing is left behind, but its cleanup is only reached after `fsio.unused_dir`, `claim`, and the first `_W.git(..., "worktree", "add", ...)` have already run. If `claim` raises after the temp path has been reserved/created (for example a CI owner-marker write fails with `OSError`), or if the add call raises unexpectedly, the generator never enters the `try`, so the `finally` block is never executed. Input: `claim=lambda p: (_ for _ in ()).throw(OSError("marker failed"))` while `fsio.unused_dir` has already created `tmp`; the context manager exits with `OSError` and leaks the scratch directory and any marker.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_locate.py:scratch_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `scratch_tree` does not canonicalize `root` to an absolute path before yielding. The cleanup in `finally` calls `_W.git(root, "worktree", "remove", ...)` and `_W.git(root, "worktree", "prune")`; if the body changes the process working directory and `root` was relative, these cleanup commands are resolved against the new cwd. Example: `with scratch_tree("repo", "HEAD"): os.chdir("/tmp")`. If `/tmp/repo` does not exist, cleanup fails and leaves a registered worktree; if `/tmp/repo` is a different repository, the prune/remove can be attempted against the wrong repository.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_locate.py:scratch_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `current` returns a `Worktree` with an empty branch when `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` fails. The code sets `branch = head.out.strip() if head.ok else ""`, then only rejects `branch == "HEAD"`. In a linked worktree whose HEAD points to a deleted branch (e.g. HEAD contains `ref: refs/heads/gone` and `refs/heads/gone` has been removed), `--show-toplevel` still succeeds, `--abbrev-ref HEAD` fails, and `current` returns `Worktree(branch="")`. Later merge code can receive an empty branch and either fail late or invoke git with an empty argument, instead of treating the tree as not adoptable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_locate.py:current

chunk_findings.detail: The function is documented as “a convenience, never a reason to fail a claim,” but it can raise `OSError` before the suppressed `ensure_ignored_dir` call. `wt_root.resolve()` and `Path(repo).resolve()` are inside a `try` that catches only `ValueError`; symlink resolution can raise `OSError` (for example, `wt_root` is a symlink loop, producing “too many levels of symbolic links”). That exception propagates and can fail the caller’s claim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_locate.py:_ignore_inside

chunk_findings.detail: When `cfg.worktree.merge_strategy == "squash"`, `git merge --squash` stages the merge result but does not leave a merge in progress on success (no `MERGE_HEAD`). If the subsequent `git commit` fails (for example, a pre-commit hook rejects it), the code runs `git reset --merge` to “unstage” the squash. Git’s `reset --merge` is only valid while a merge is in progress, so in this state it fails; the function then reports that unstaging failed and tells the user to run the same invalid `git reset --merge` by hand. The staged squash remains in the index, contrary to the stated cleanup and with a risk that a later commit picks it up. A plain `git reset`/`git reset HEAD` is the correct unstage here.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_merge.py:_merge_here

chunk_findings.detail: `commit()` stages the requested paths (or `-u`) and then runs `git commit -m body` with no pathspec, and it ignores the result of the `git add` call. Given a worktree whose index already contains an unrelated staged file, calling `commit(wt, "msg", ["missing.txt"])` makes `git add -- missing.txt` fail, but the function still proceeds to `git commit` and commits the unrelated staged file. Even when `git add` succeeds, any unrelated file already in the index is included. This directly contradicts the function’s stated guarantee that explicit paths prevent another agent’s unrelated staged file from entering the commit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_merge.py:commit

chunk_findings.detail: In the forced-removal path, if `git worktree remove --force` fails while `wt.path` exists, the code calls `shutil.rmtree(wt.path, ignore_errors=True)` and then unconditionally returns `GitResult(0, "removed (pruned)", "")`. If the directory cannot be removed (permissions, read-only filesystem, symlink/mount-point, etc.), `rmtree` ignores the error and the worktree remains, but the caller is told the removal succeeded. It also ignores the result of `git worktree prune`, so metadata can remain while the function reports success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_merge.py:remove

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_decls` submodule is reported as defining `_one_of`, but the package initializer re-exports `strictest` and the other `_decls` names while omitting `_one_of`. Because the change is intended to preserve every `from ddflow.config import X` call site, any existing site such as `from ddflow.config import _one_of` (valid when `_one_of` was a top-level name in `ddflow/config.py`) now raises `ImportError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/__init__.py:128

chunk_findings.detail: The type dispatch checks scalar element names (`"bool"`, `"int"`, `"float"`) before checking for a list container, so any list-of-scalar annotation is coerced as if it were the scalar itself. Given a knob declared `list[int]` (or string annotation `"list[int]"`) and env/file value `"1,2"`, `_coerce` enters the `if "int" in ts` branch and calls `int("1,2")`, raising `ValueError`/`InvalidValue` even though the value is a valid comma-separated list of ints. With value `"1"`, it returns `1`, not `[1]`. The same applies to `list[bool]`: raw `"true"` returns `True`, not `[True]`, and raw `"true,false"` raises “not a boolean” instead of producing `[True, False]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_coerce.py:_coerce

chunk_findings.detail: For the `k=v,k=v` dict notation, pairs are filtered using `p.strip()` but then split without stripping each pair, so whitespace after commas becomes part of keys or values. Given a `dict[str, str]` knob and raw value `"core=core, reviewer=reviewer"`, this returns `{"core": "core", " reviewer": "reviewer"}` (note the leading space in the second key), rather than stripping to `{"core": "core", "reviewer": "reviewer"}`. A consumer matching exact family names, such as the reviewer-independence check mentioned in the comments, can silently miss the spaced key.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_coerce.py:_coerce_dict

chunk_findings.detail: This new submodule in the bottom `config` layer imports from the sibling package `..config_sections._compat`. That makes `ddflow.config` depend on another ddflow package/layer (`config_sections`), directly violating the stated layering rule that `config` imports no other layer. Because `ddflow/config/__init__.py` re-exports the package API, merely importing `ddflow.config` executes this import; `tests/test_layering.py` should flag it, and if `config_sections` imports any part of `ddflow.config`, it also creates a circular import at package initialization.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_warn.py:8

chunk_findings.detail: The re-export table is incomplete for `_locate.py`. The split manifest says `_locate.py` defines top-level `error`, but `_SUBMODULE_OF` has no `"error"` entry and `error` is not one of the eager globals in this `__init__.py`. Therefore, after the split, `from ddflow.infra.worktree import error` or `W.error` after `import ddflow.infra.worktree as W` goes through `__getattr__`, finds no mapping, and raises `AttributeError`. Before the split that name was part of the old module’s top-level namespace, so callers or tests importing/monkeypatching `error` break, contradicting the file’s claim that the public API is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/__init__.py:_SUBMODULE_OF

chunk_findings.detail: The package uses PEP 562 lazy `__getattr__` re-exports but does not define `__all__`. Python’s `from module import *` does not consult `__getattr__` when `__all__` is absent; it only copies names already present in the module’s globals. Thus `from ddflow.infra.worktree import *` will not bind lazy public names such as `create`, `remove`, `merge`, or `sync`, even if those names were accessed earlier (because `__getattr__` does not insert them into globals). The old single-module version would have exported those top-level public names under star import, and the new package also leaks new globals such as `G` and `importlib` into star-importing namespaces.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/__init__.py:_SUBMODULE_OF

chunk_findings.detail: The adoption path returns as soon as `path/.git` exists, without checking that the existing worktree is actually on the requested `branch`. For example, if an item’s worktree already exists and its `HEAD` is on `feature/old`, a later call such as `create(repo, cfg, item_id, branch="feature/new")` (e.g. after a config change to `cfg.worktree.branch_prefix` or an explicit caller-supplied branch) returns a `Worktree` whose `branch` field is `"feature/new"` while the checked-out branch remains `"feature/old"`. Any subsequent operation that trusts `wt.branch` (merge, branch checks, etc.) will then operate on the wrong branch or on a branch that does not exist in that worktree. An idempotent create should either return the actual checked-out branch or reject/adjust when it differs from the requested branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:39-42

chunk_findings.detail: The return values of the `git add -N` call on line 44 and the `git reset` cleanup on line 67 are ignored, unlike `_diff_text`, which checks `r.ok` and raises. If `git add -N` fails for any reason (for example, an untracked path cannot be added because of a filesystem permission or ignore/index issue), `capture_diff` still proceeds and returns a diff that omits those new files, silently violating the docstring’s “failure is never an empty ‘nothing changed’” contract. If `git add -N` succeeds but `git reset` fails afterward (for example, another process acquires `index.lock` during the diff), the function still returns normally while leaving intent-to-add entries in the index, so a later commit can include those previously untracked files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:44 (capture_diff)

chunk_findings.detail: The lossy-name matching double-counts diff sections. `shown` treats an exact path as covered, but `room` is initialized from all `seen.count(name)` occurrences without subtracting changed paths that are already exactly shown. Given two changed files whose status paths are `a\ufffd` (a valid file name containing U+FFFD) and `a\udcff` (a raw non-UTF-8 byte that `lossy()` maps to `a\ufffd`), if the diff contains only one section for `a\ufffd` and omits the raw-byte file, then `absent == [a\udcff]`, `room["a\ufffd"] == 1`, and the loop consumes that section for the absent path. The function returns `(True, [])`, even though the diff has one section but two changed paths needing coverage.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:118 (diff_covers_everything)

chunk_findings.detail: The filter `if p.strip()` drops valid paths whose names consist only of whitespace. Given an untracked file named `" "`, `G.files` returns `" "`, `p.strip()` is empty, and the path is excluded from `untracked_files`; therefore `capture_diff` never intent-to-adds it and omits it from the review diff. Meanwhile `_status_paths` keeps the path because it filters only with `if p`, so `diff_covers_everything` would report it as missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_diff.py:91 (untracked_files)

chunk_findings.detail: `tracks_local_file` passes `name` to `git ls-files` as a pathspec, so git glob magic is interpreted. On a primary checkout that tracks `pyproject.toml` and contains an untracked local file literally named `*.toml`, `copy_local_files_report(..., names=['*.toml'])` runs `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- *.toml`; the pattern matches the tracked `pyproject.toml`, `.ok` is true, and the untracked file is reported `SKIP_TRACKED` and not copied. The same pathspec treatment can also make a tracked file whose literal name contains `[...]` look untracked. The check needs a literal pathspec (e.g. `:(literal)<name>`) or equivalent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_local.py:13

chunk_findings.detail: The failure cleanup assumes `dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)` cannot raise, but it can when the failure was not a half-written file. If the primary has an untracked `sub/file` and the tree already has a regular file at `tree/sub`, `dst.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)` raises `FileExistsError` (an `OSError`); the handler then calls `dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)` on `tree/sub/file`, which raises `NotADirectoryError` because a path component is a file, not `FileNotFoundError`, so `missing_ok` does not suppress it. The function propagates instead of returning `SKIP_FAILED`, killing the caller despite the doc's promise that a failed convenience copy must not kill the claim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_local.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_local_files` uses the report dict, but duplicate entries in `names` collapse to one key and the later status overwrites the earlier one. With primary containing an untracked file `a`, tree lacking `a`, and `names=['a', 'a']`, the first iteration copies `a` and stores `None`; the second sees the destination exists and overwrites the entry with `SKIP_PRESENT`. `copy_local_files` therefore returns `[]` even though `a` was actually copied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_local.py:78

chunk_findings.detail: `scratch_tree` stores `root = Path(root)` but does not resolve it, while cleanup later runs `_W.git(root, ...)` after the body may have changed the process working directory. If the caller passes a relative root (the signature accepts `Path | str` and does not require absolute paths) and the body does `os.chdir(...)`, the `finally` block runs `git worktree remove` and `git worktree prune` in the new cwd, not in the repository that owns the scratch worktree. For example, `with scratch_tree(Path('.'), 'HEAD'): os.chdir('/tmp')` causes cleanup to execute in `/tmp`; if `/tmp` is not the original repository, the remove/prune commands fail or act on the wrong repository, leaving the original repository's worktree registration behind despite the docstring’s “whatever the body did” promise.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_locate.py:scratch_tree

chunk_findings.detail: The `claim` callback is invoked before the `try`/`finally` block, so any exception raised by `claim` bypasses all cleanup. A claim implementation that writes its owner marker and then raises (for example, a transient error after `marker.write_text(...)`) leaves the reserved temporary directory and/or marker on disk. The docstring states that nothing is left behind and that the returned marker path is unlinked on exit, but the code only performs that unlink after `claim` has returned successfully.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_locate.py:scratch_tree

chunk_findings.detail: In the squash path, after `git merge --squash` returns success the code decides whether to commit by checking `git diff --cached --quiet`, then runs `git commit -m message` if the cached diff is non-empty. That cached diff includes any pre-existing staged changes in the target tree, not only changes produced by the merge. Because `_merge_here` is allowed to run in the primary checkout without a staged-file guard, this can commit unrelated work: with target `main` checked out in the primary, `notes.md` already staged, and a source branch already merged into `main`, `git merge --squash` is a no-op but leaves `notes.md` staged; the subsequent commit creates a commit on `main` containing `notes.md`. This is the unrelated-file corruption the module’s own docstring warns about.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_merge.py:_merge_here

chunk_findings.detail: `commit()` ignores the result of `git add`. If `paths=["typo.txt"]` is passed, `git add -- typo.txt` fails (e.g. pathspec does not match or path is ignored), but the function still runs `git commit -m body`. If the worktree already has staged unrelated files, the commit succeeds and includes those unrelated staged files; if there are no staged files, the caller receives a generic “nothing to commit” failure instead of the actual `git add` pathspec error. The explicit-paths contract is broken because add failures are not propagated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_merge.py:commit

chunk_findings.detail: When `force=True` and `git worktree remove --force` fails, the function calls `shutil.rmtree(wt.path, ignore_errors=True)` and then unconditionally returns `G.GitResult(0, "removed (pruned)", "")`. Because `ignore_errors=True` suppresses real removal failures such as permission errors, the directory may still exist while `remove()` reports success. For example, a worktree containing a read-only/locked subdirectory can survive both the git removal and the ignored `rmtree`, but the function still claims the worktree was removed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_merge.py:remove

chunk_findings.detail: `load_path` decides “absolute” with the platform-specific `Path(stored).is_absolute()`. A log written on Windows can contain an absolute path such as `C:\repo\wt` (the different-drive fallback in `store_path` returns `str(p)` with backslashes, and older Windows logs may contain such paths). If that log is loaded on Linux/CI/container, `Path("C:\repo\wt").is_absolute()` is False, so line 51 reinterprets it as repo-relative and returns `Path(repo) / "C:\repo\wt"` instead of honouring the stored absolute path. That contradicts the docstring’s stated guarantee and can make recovery/`absolutise` look at a nonexistent subdirectory of the repository rather than the real worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_paths.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: This new submodule in the bottom `config` layer imports from the sibling package `..config_sections._compat`. That makes `ddflow.config` depend on another ddflow package/layer (`config_sections`), directly violating the stated layering rule that `config` imports no other layer. Because `ddflow/config/__init__.py` re-exports the package API, merely importing `ddflow.config` executes this import; `tests/test_layering.py` should flag it, and if `config_sections` imports any part of `ddflow.config`, it also creates a circular import at package initialization.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_warn.py:8

evidence.diff_source: delta review of 1 commit since d448561b2c

chunk_findings.detail: The file `ddflow/infra/store.py` has been deleted entirely from the repository without providing its implementation in the manifest files for this part (nor is it listed under any non-existent new file except as deleted: `ddflow/infra/store.py (+0 -1605): deleted`), which breaks all external imports of `ddflow.infra.store` and makes the package unimportable and broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store.py

chunk_findings.detail:
The inline-YAML parser splits on commas after stripping quotes, so it corrupts valid quoted scalars that contain commas. Given a `.aider.conf.yml` containing exactly:

```yaml
read: ["foo, bar"]
```

and no `AGENTS.md` entry, `_add_aider_read` calls `_aider_read_values`, which sees the bracketed text `"foo, bar"`, splits it on `,`, and returns the two values `foo` and `bar`. `_add_aider_read` then rewrites the file as a block list:

```yaml
read:
  - foo
  - bar
  - AGENTS.md
```

YAML originally meant one list item, `foo, bar`; after adoption Aider is told to load `foo` and `bar`. The same normalization also breaks values containing `#` because the block entries are written unquoted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:_aider_read_values

chunk_findings.detail: `adopt` can overwrite an existing native rules file for a newly adopted agent without making the backup it promises. `_backup_docs` is called before the per-agent delta files are written, and it decides what to back up from `rules_status` / `adopted_agents`, which only see deltas already present on disk. If a project already has a native rules file such as `.cursor/rules/ddflow.mdc`, but has no `docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/cursor.md`, then `adopt(repo, ["cursor"])` does not include `.cursor/rules/ddflow.mdc` in the backup set. Later in the same call, `_write_native_rule` for Cursor uses `FORM_WHOLE` and replaces the whole file with `native_rule_text(...)`, destroying any hand-written Cursor rules with no `.ddflow/backups` entry and no `.local-edits` copy.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_adopt.py:adopt

chunk_findings.detail: The manual-registration message ignores `docs_dir`. `_DOCS_HINT` is hardcoded to `"docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/"`, while `adopt` accepts a custom `docs_dir`. Given `adopt(repo, ["some-agent-with-no-mcp-config"], docs_dir="docs/flow")`, the driver deltas are written under `docs/flow/drivers/deltas/`, but the returned action tells the operator to consult `docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/`, which is the wrong path and may not exist.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_adopt.py:_register_mcp

chunk_findings.detail: The public `adopt` signature still accepts `force`, but the function body never references it. Every operation that can touch existing files is called without any force argument: `init_files(repo)`, `_backup_docs(..., None)`, `_upsert_block(path, section, name)`, and `E.install(repo)`. As a result, `adopt(repo, ["claude"], force=True)` behaves exactly like `force=False`; a caller that relies on `--force` to overwrite existing managed blocks or scaffold files gets no forcing (or still hits the non-forced/refusal path). Since the stated intent is a pure split preserving the old public behavior, dropping the `force` plumbing is a behavioral defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_adopt.py:24 (`adopt` `force` parameter)

chunk_findings.detail:
The inline alternative in `_AIDER_LISTED` is not restricted to the actual `read:` inline list; it matches any bracketed `AGENTS.md` after `read:` on the same line, including YAML comments, and its `\b` boundary also matches filenames that merely start with `AGENTS.md`. For example, given `.aider.conf.yml`:
```yaml
read: [CONVENTIONS.md] # see [AGENTS.md]
```
`_aider_lists_agents_md` returns True because the match is in the comment, so `_add_aider_read` returns “already loads” and never adds `AGENTS.md` to the real `read:` list. Likewise, `read: [AGENTS.md.bak]` matches because `\b` allows the `.bak` suffix, so a backup file is treated as the required instruction file. This is a silent no-op for Aider wiring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:26

chunk_findings.detail:
`_add_aider_read` consumes following block sequence entries only if they have at least one whitespace character before `-` (`^\s+-`). YAML permits a block sequence under a mapping key to be at the same indentation as the key, e.g.:
```yaml
read:
- CONVENTIONS.md
```
For this valid input, `_aider_lists_agents_md` is False, `_aider_read_values` returns no existing values, and the loop consumes nothing because `- CONVENTIONS.md` does not match `^\s+-`. The replacement becomes:
```yaml
read:
  - AGENTS.md
- CONVENTIONS.md
```
which is invalid YAML / changes the document structure and loses the operator’s existing entry.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:73

chunk_findings.detail:
`_aider_read_values` parses YAML-ish text with ad-hoc splits that ignore quoting. If the `read:` line is a quoted scalar containing `#`, e.g.:
```yaml
read: "file#1.md"
```
line 102 treats the `#` inside the quotes as a comment start, returning value `"file` and trailing comment ` #1.md"`. `_add_aider_read` then writes:
```yaml
read: #1.md"
  - "file
  - AGENTS.md
```
corrupting the original entry. The same class of bug appears for inline lists: `read: ["a,b.md"]` is split on the comma inside the quoted scalar and rewritten as two entries (`a` and `b.md`) plus `AGENTS.md`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:98

chunk_findings.detail:
The block-form alternative in `_AIDER_LISTED` requires the line to end immediately after `AGENTS.md`, so valid block entries with trailing comments or quotes are not recognized as already loaded. Given:
```yaml
read:
  - AGENTS.md # required
```
`_aider_lists_agents_md` returns False. `_add_aider_read` then parses the existing entry as `AGENTS.md # required` and appends another unquoted `AGENTS.md`, duplicating the entry instead of returning the idempotent “already loads” result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_aider.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: In `_write_command`, a malformed managed region is explicitly caught at line 145 and commented as “a broken region is the operator's file: leave it alone” (line 146). However, if that broken file still contains `MANAGED_MARK`, the code does not leave it alone: the `MANAGED_MARK not in existing` guard at line 149 is false, so control falls through to line 156 and calls `replace_text(...)`, overwriting the file without going through `_update_managed` and without creating a `local_edits_path` backup. For example, if `.claude/commands/implement.md` contains a begin marker such as `<!-- DDFLOW:MANAGED commands/implement -->` but the end marker was edited away, `region.owns(existing)` raises `RegionError`, `owned` becomes false, and adoption destroys the operator’s `/implement` workflow despite the code’s stated contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_commands.py:146-156

chunk_findings.detail: `_driver_pairs` treats every `*.md` entry in `<docs_dir>/drivers/deltas` as a driver document as long as a matching template exists, without checking that the project-side path is a regular file. `Path.glob` yields directories and broken symlinks as well as files. For example, in an adopted project where `docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/cursor.md` is a broken symlink (or a directory) and `templates/drivers/deltas/cursor.md` exists, `driver_states` calls `mine.read_text("utf-8", errors="replace")` on that path, raising `FileNotFoundError`/`IsADirectoryError`. Consequently `driver_drift` and `refresh_docs` crash instead of ignoring a non-existent driver doc, contradicting the docstring’s “driver doc that EXISTS”. The loop should filter `path.is_file()` (in addition to `tmpl.is_file()`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_docs.py:33 (`_driver_pairs`)

chunk_findings.detail: When `ddflow` is running from a source checkout (`_running_from_source()` is true), but there is no `uvx` or `ddflow-mcp` on `PATH` and `docker` is installed, `_launch_entry("auto")` returns the Docker entry. The Docker branch is entered without checking `_running_from_source()` (unlike the `uvx` and `ddflow-mcp` branches) and it comes before the “source checkout: point at THIS tree” fallback. For example, on a developer machine with Docker but no `uvx`/`ddflow-mcp`, `_launch_entry("auto")` returns `{"command": "docker", "args": [..., "ghcr.io/OWNER/ddflow:latest"]}` instead of a Python entry using the local checkout. That configures the project to run the published/placeholder Docker image rather than the code the developer is editing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_launch.py:_launch_entry

chunk_findings.detail: `has_legacy_block` and `block_body` detect the legacy managed block by substring search (`LEGACY_BEGIN in text` / `text.index(...)`), while `block_spans` and the writer treat markers as whole-line markers. Given an `AGENTS.md` that contains a real legacy block but has an earlier documentation line mentioning `<!-- DDFLOW:END -->`, `block_body` finds that prose `LEGACY_END` before the first `LEGACY_BEGIN`, raises `RegionError`, and `_block_state` turns that into `NO_BLOCK`; `rules_status` then reports the ddflow section as removed even though the block exists. Conversely, a file with no managed block but a single line mentioning both legacy markers in order is treated as a legacy block and reported `STALE`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_rules.py:has_legacy_block

chunk_findings.detail: For `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, `rules_status` checks `path.exists()` and then calls `path.read_text(...)` without catching `OSError`. If `repo/AGENTS.md` is a directory (or a symlink to a directory), `exists()` returns `True`, `read_text` raises `IsADirectoryError`, and the whole status check crashes instead of returning a `RulesState`. The native-rule loop below uses `path.is_file()`, so this path is inconsistent and can make a rules-status call fail on an otherwise inspectable filesystem state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_rules.py:rules_status

chunk_findings.detail: The package initializer imports `_Parsed`, `_Delta`, and `_MERGED` from `._parse`, but it does not import or re-export `_Merged`, which the change manifest explicitly says `_parse.py` adds. Since the old `ddflow.infra.log` module exposed `_Merged`, an unchanged call site such as `from ddflow.infra.log import _Merged` now raises `ImportError: cannot import name '_Merged'`. This breaks the stated no-behavior-change/unchanged-call-sites requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/__init__.py (import block from `._parse`)

chunk_findings.detail: The function’s own docstring says `DDFLOW_AGENT` overrides the derived identity, but the implementation never reads `os.environ` or `DDFLOW_AGENT`. Given `DDFLOW_AGENT=worker-1 default_agent_id(fallback_root=repo)`, the code returns `host-tree-suffix` instead of `worker-1`, so the documented escape hatch for multiple agents in one tree does not work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_agent.py:default_agent_id

chunk_findings.detail: When `fallback_root` is omitted, `root` is `""`, so `_clone_suffix` is never called and the returned id has no clone suffix. In an adopted checkout, `default_agent_id()` therefore returns `host-<checkout>` instead of the documented `host-<checkout>-<clone-suffix>`. This can reintroduce the B190 cross-clone collision merely because the caller used the default argument.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_agent.py:default_agent_id

chunk_findings.detail: The initial `with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError): return path.read_text("utf-8").strip()` is outside the later `try/except OSError`. If `.ddflow/local/clone-id` exists but is unreadable (for example after being restored with mode `000`), `read_text` raises `PermissionError`, which is not caught, so `default_agent_id` crashes instead of falling back to an unsuffixed or safe identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_agent.py:_clone_suffix

chunk_findings.detail: `_linked_tree_here` verifies only that a stored relative worktree path resolves to a linked worktree in this clone’s `git worktree list`; it cannot distinguish this clone from a teammate whose event records the same relative worktree string (e.g. both have `../feature`). If this clone’s `.ddflow/events` contains a merged teammate shard and the clone-id file is deleted, `_recovered_suffix` can adopt the teammate’s suffix and give this clone the same identity as that teammate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_agent.py:_linked_tree_here/_recovered_suffix

chunk_findings.detail: `append_many` is documented as all-or-nothing, and specifically that "a reader never sees half of a merge or a split", but the code writes and `fsync`s each event one at a time while readers take no lock. A concurrent reader that reads the shard after the first `_write` returns but before the second starts will see only the first event, even when the second event later succeeds. The input is two valid kinds; process A pauses inside `append_many` between the two appends while process B calls `read_all` and observes the half-written unit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py:append_many

chunk_findings.detail: The rollback path for a failed `append_many` only `os.truncate`s the current shard and restores `_lamport`; it does not undo the earlier `_meta.advance` and `APPEND_HOOKS` side effects made by an event that was already written before a later item raised. For `[("valid","s",{}), ("__no_such_kind__","s",{})]`, the first event has already been passed to `services.shardmarks` high-water-mark bookkeeping before the second raises `ValueError`; after truncation that high-water mark is past EOF. If no shard existed before the call, the rollback also leaves an empty `.jsonl`, so the state is not "none" as guaranteed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py:append_many

chunk_findings.detail: `_held_key` builds the re-entrancy guard key from `str(path)` without canonicalizing the path (`resolve()`/realpath). `flock` is per open-file-description, so a second `os.open` of the same lock file through a different spelling of the path — e.g. `Path("repo/.ddflow/log.lock")` held by thread T, then a nested transaction through `Path("repo/.ddflow/log.lock").resolve()` — produces a different key in `_HELD`. The second acquisition therefore opens the same file again and blocks or times out against the lock T already holds. The guard’s own comment says two EventLog objects for one repo is the exact same-thread re-entry case this key exists to handle, so the key must use a canonical file identity, not the raw path string.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_lock.py:_held_key

chunk_findings.detail: `_snapshot_frame` is the validation gate documented to dismiss a malformed frame and degrade to a slower read. It only checks that `tuples` is a `list`, not that each element is a tuple matching `_EVENT_FIELDS`. A malformed frame such as `(10, "abc", 0, [1, 2])` is returned as valid; when the snapshot-seeding code later tries to rebuild `Event` objects from that list, the bad element escapes as a trusted event tuple and can raise instead of being ignored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_parse.py:_snapshot_frame

chunk_findings.detail: `_parser_stamp` claims to fingerprint the code that turns a line into an `Event`, but it hashes only code objects, `co_consts`, and `co_names`. `_recover_glued` depends on the module-global `_LINE_START`; changing that value changes recovery behavior, yet the fingerprint is unchanged because only the name `_LINE_START`, not its bound string value, is hashed. A snapshot written under the old marker can therefore be reused under a parser with different recovery behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_parse.py:_parser_stamp

chunk_findings.detail:
The bounded tail reader can silently return `""` even when a final non-empty line exists. With the documented 64 KiB `TAIL_MAX_BYTES`, take a file of size 65537: `b"a
" + b"b"*65535`. At the last loop iteration `window = 65536`, `fh.seek(1)` reads `b"
" + b"b"*65535`; after `split(b"
")` and filtering empty segments, only the final `b` line remains, so `len(lines) > 1` is false and `size <= window` is false (65537 > 65536). The loop exits and returns `""`, despite the final non-empty line being shorter than the bound.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_last_line

chunk_findings.detail: The package facade re-exports names by importing them from submodules, so the callables keep their submodule globals and `__module__`. This is an observable behavior change from the old flat module. For example, `import ddflow.api.rules as R; R.rule_add.__module__` is now `ddflow.api.rules.add`, not `ddflow.api.rules`, so introspection that filters API members by `__module__ == "ddflow.api.rules"` now sees none of the operations. More importantly, rebinding a helper on the package no longer affects the moved functions: `R._check_edit = lambda *a, **k: None; R.rule_update(...)` (or `mock.patch("ddflow.api.rules.DEFAULT_RULE_PRIORITY", ...)`) changes the package attribute, but `rule_update`/`rules_manifest` resolve `_check_edit`/`DEFAULT_RULE_PRIORITY` in `ddflow.api.rules.mutate`/`write`, so the original object is used. Existing tests or runtime monkeypatches that targeted `ddflow.api.rules` helpers/constants will silently become ineffective, contradicting the claimed no-behavior-change refactor.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rules/__init__.py:13-31

chunk_findings.detail: The old module lived in package `ddflow.surfaces`, so `from ..config_sections._compat import MIN_REMOVED_IN, check_rename` resolved to `ddflow.config_sections._compat`, and `from .argtypes import glob_list_hint` resolved to `ddflow.surfaces.argtypes`. The new submodules live in `ddflow.surfaces.registry`, one package level deeper. Keeping the same relative prefixes as the change description says (`..config_sections._compat` and `.argtypes`) now resolves `..config_sections._compat` to `ddflow.surfaces.config_sections._compat` (not the original `ddflow.config_sections._compat`) and `.argtypes` to `ddflow.surfaces.registry.argtypes`. The registry package has no `argtypes.py` in the manifest, so `import ddflow.surfaces.registry` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`; the relative imports must gain one dot (`...config_sections._compat` and `..argtypes`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry/_aliases.py and ddflow/surfaces/registry/__init__.py imports

chunk_findings.detail: The override calls `super().__call__(parser, namespace, values, option_string)` but does not return its result. `argparse._SubParsersAction.__call__` returns `(namespace, arg_strings)`, and `argparse` unpacks that return value while parsing a subparsers action. Returning `None` instead makes every subcommand parse fail; for example, parsing any real CLI invocation with a subcommand (such as `ddflow task list`) hits `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry/__init__.py:_WordsRecorder.__call__

chunk_findings.detail: The import uses `from ...config_sections._compat import ...`. In the new package layout, `_aliases.py` is in package `ddflow.surfaces.registry`, so three dots resolve to `ddflow.config_sections._compat`. But `config_sections` is at the surfaces layer (`ddflow.surfaces.config_sections`), as the change description requires (`..config_sections._compat`). Importing this module will raise `ModuleNotFoundError` for `ddflow.config_sections`, so the split package cannot even load.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry/_aliases.py:14

chunk_findings.detail: `exclusive_required=True` is documented as making the mutually exclusive group required, but `add_to` creates groups with `parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()` and never passes `required=self.exclusive_required` (and never otherwise uses that field). For example, with `groups = {}`, `Param(name="mode", exclusive="action", exclusive_required=True).add_to(parser, groups)` followed by `Param(name="list", exclusive="action").add_to(parser, groups)`, `parser.parse_args([])` succeeds with both attributes `None`, even though exactly one of `--mode`/`--list` must be given.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry/_param.py:Param.add_to

chunk_findings.detail: For `Param(name="tag", repeat=True, choices=("a", "b"), schema_enum=True)`, `schemaschema()` returns `{"type": "array", "description": "", "items": {"type": "string"}, "enum": ["a", "b"]}`. In JSON Schema 2020-12 the property must satisfy both `type: "array"` and `enum: ["a", "b"]`, so the valid CLI list `["a"]` fails validation; for array parameters the choices enum belongs under `items`, not on the array itself.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry/_param.py:Param.schema

chunk_findings.detail: `result_schemas` calls `array_schema(command, payload)` without passing the tool's `text` indicator. Given a tool spec such as `{"payload": "hits", "text": True}`, `result_shape(payload, text=text)` correctly reports `"shape": "text"`, but `array_schema` calls `result_shape(payload)` with `text=False`, sees `"hits"` in `ARRAY_PAYLOADS`, and returns a non-null array schema. The emitted table then pins both `"shape": "text"` and an `"array_schema"` document for a text result. `array_schema` should receive/pass the same `text` value so it only emits an array schema when the actual result shape is `"array"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry/_schemas.py:139 result_schemas

chunk_findings.detail: The new package exposes the old module’s public names lazily through `__getattr__` and `__dir__`. That does not reproduce the old top-level module’s star-import behavior. The deleted `progress.py` had no `__all__`, so `from ddflow.core.progress import *` bound every public name (`detect`, `work`, `LoopFinding`, etc.). In a package whose public names are only returned by `__getattr__` and listed by `__dir__`, `import *` without `__all__` reads the package namespace, not `__getattr__` or `__dir__`; on a fresh import the namespace contains only the lazy machinery, so `from ddflow.core.progress import *; detect(...)` raises `NameError`. Any caller or test that used star import loses the API after the refactor.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/progress/__init__.py

chunk_findings.detail: Splitting the module changes which global namespace the moved functions use, so patching the old `ddflow.core.progress` attribute no longer changes calls made inside the package. In the deleted module, `detect`, `work`, and imported helpers such as `find_cycles` were globals of one module; setting `ddflow.core.progress.work = fake` or `ddflow.core.progress.find_cycles = lambda items: []` changed what `detect` called. After the split, `detect` lives in `ddflow.core.progress.loops` and calls `work`/`find_cycles` resolved from that submodule’s globals, while assigning the old top-level attribute only changes the package namespace. For example, `progress.work = lambda events, state: {}` followed by `progress.detect(events, state, cfg)` still runs the real `work` from `tracking` and can produce unexpected findings, whereas the old module used the patched `work`. This is a regression in the monkeypatch/hook API unless every existing patch target was moved to the new submodule paths, which the manifest does not show.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/progress/loops.py:detect

chunk_findings.detail: The lazy re-export proxies only reads. Assigning a name on the package (`monkeypatch.setattr(progress, "_static_cycles", fake)`, `progress.REVIEW_GATES = ...`, etc.) stores the value in the package `__dict__`; it does not update the globals of the submodule where the moved function actually resolves its names. In the old single-file module, patching or overriding `_static_cycles`, `REVIEW_GATES`, or similar names on `ddflow.core.progress` changed the globals used by `detect` and the other functions. After the split, `progress.detect` (defined in `ddflow/core/progress/loops.py`) still sees the original submodule globals, so a test or runtime configuration that patches/overrides those names on the package silently continues to use the old values. This is a behavior regression relative to the stated monkeypatch invariant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/progress/__init__.py:58 (`__getattr__`)

chunk_findings.detail: Moving `_offload` from `ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py` into `ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_offload.py` changes the meaning of the repository-root calculation `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`. In the old module that expression was the checkout/site-packages root; in the new package submodule it is the `ddflow` package directory itself. When an offloaded tool such as `ddflow_gate_run` is called and the server process’s cwd does not already make `ddflow` importable, `_offload` puts the package directory on `PYTHONPATH`; the spawned worker `python -c "from ddflow.surfaces.mcp import _worker_main as m; m()"` then fails to import `ddflow` with `ModuleNotFoundError`, whereas the old single-module path succeeded. The root must be computed one level higher (`parents[3]`, or from the package parent) to preserve behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_offload.py:_offload

chunk_findings.detail: The old deferred-import baseline for the monolithic `ddflow.surfaces.mcp` module was deleted, but `_finish_list_read`—listed as moving to `ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_reply.py`—still performs lazy `importlib.import_module` calls for `ddflow.api.viewers`, `ddflow.core.outcome`, and `ddflow.api.knowledge.bugs`. The manifest adds a deferred-imports baseline only for `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._core`, not for `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._reply`, so running the deferred-imports guard ratchet on the new submodule reports unbaselined lazy imports that were previously baselined under the old module.
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/deferred_imports/ddflow.surfaces.mcp._reply.toml

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest states that `ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_serve.py` adds top-level `notify` alongside `serve`, `_reexec_ready`, and `main`, but this package `__init__` imports only `_reexec_ready`, `main`, and `serve`. After the split, an existing import site such as `from ddflow.surfaces.mcp import notify` or an attribute access `ddflow.surfaces.mcp.notify(...)` fails with `ImportError`/`AttributeError`, contradicting the stated intent that old import sites keep working unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp/__init__.py: `from ._serve import _reexec_ready, main, serve`

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest states that `ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_offload.py` adds top-level `relay` in addition to `_offloaded`, `_worker_stderr`, `_offload`, and three more symbols. The `__init__` re-export block imports `MAX_WORKERS`, `_frame_writer`, `_offload`, `_offloaded`, `_worker_main`, and `_worker_stderr`, but omits `relay`. Therefore code that previously did `from ddflow.surfaces.mcp import relay` or accessed `ddflow.surfaces.mcp.relay` now fails after the module was split into a package.

chunk_findings.detail: The deferred-import ratchet baseline was not moved for this submodule. `_reply.py` still performs lazy imports in `_finish_list_read` (`importlib.import_module("ddflow.api.viewers")`, `importlib.import_module("ddflow.core.outcome")`, and `importlib.import_module("ddflow.api.knowledge.bugs")`), but the manifest deletes the old `tests/guard_baselines/deferred_imports/ddflow.surfaces.mcp.toml` and adds a baseline only for `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._core`. Running the deferred-import guard on this tree therefore sees unbaselined deferred imports in `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._reply` (or silently ratchets them away), contradicting the change’s stated goal of preserving the existing guard baseline exactly across the split.

chunk_findings.detail: `inp = stdin or _upgrade.stdio_lines()` conflates a valid but falsey stdin iterable with the `None` sentinel. For example, calling `serve(repo, stdin=[], stdout=io.StringIO())` should consume the caller-supplied empty stream and return at EOF, but `[]` is falsey, so line 47 substitutes `_upgrade.stdio_lines()` and reads the process’s real stdin. In an MCP session where stdin is an open pipe, the server then blocks waiting for input instead of honoring the caller’s empty stream. The sentinel check should test `stdin is not None`.

chunk_findings.detail: The combined `ignore_imports` baseline for the `surfaces-through-api` contract grows from four entries in the deleted `ddflow.surfaces.mcp.toml` to six entries across the new submodule baselines: `harness_identity` is now allowed from both `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._handlers` and `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._server`, and `proc` is now allowed from both `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._offload` and `ddflow.surfaces.mcp._serve`. The new baseline files themselves state that these entries “only shrink, never grow,” but the change increases the allowed direct `ddflow.infra` imports for the contract; if the architecture guard aggregates the baselines for the contract as a whole, this ratchet regression will fail the guard test.
