chunk_findings.detail: The predicate decides solely from the caller-supplied `target` string: it splits it and checks those gate ids are unavailable/partial. It never verifies that the target is the full set of required gates left unmet by the completion verdict. If a `complete.force` ask/request is evaluated with a target that names only one of the unmet gates, e.g. `target="lint"` while the verdict's `unmet_gates` are `["unit_tests", "lint"]`, with `unit_tests` recorded `failed` and `lint` recorded `unavailable`, the predicate returns `True` and the standing rule auto-answers `complete.force`, allowing completion despite a genuinely failed required gate. The intent requires *all* unmet required gates to be unavailable/partial; this code only guarantees the gates that happen to be in `target`, so a failed/silent gate can be omitted and bypassed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:_unavailable_unmet_only

chunk_findings.detail: The new calls pass gate-state strings where the helper expects a gate id: `_only_unavailable_gate(proj, "failed")`, `_only_unavailable_gate(repo, unit)` inside `_only_unavailable_repo`, and `_only_unavailable_gate(proj, "unavailable")` in the window-lapse test. For example, `_only_unavailable_repo(repo, "unavailable")` configures the pipeline as `implement,unit_tests,merge`, then calls `_only_unavailable_gate(repo, "unavailable")`; since the second positional argument is a gate id, this marks a gate named `unavailable` unavailable instead of marking `unit_tests` unavailable. The end-to-end test then runs `ddflow complete T1` and asserts success because “the only unmet required gate is `unit_tests=unavailable`”, but the real `unit_tests` gate is still not set to unavailable, so the standing-rule predicate does not see the intended only-unavailable blocker and the CLI can exit with the refusal code, making the test fail (or, if the helper replaces the only required gate, it passes while exercising a nonexistent gate rather than `unit_tests`). This is the previously reported misuse still present in the added/edited lines.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_policy.py:_only_unavailable_gate

chunk_findings.detail: `_only_unavailable_gate(proj, "failed")` still passes a state literal as the helper’s second argument, but that parameter is the gate id in `_only_unavailable_gate`. The same defect is repeated at lines 251 (`_only_unavailable_gate(repo, unit)`, fed by `"unavailable"`/`"failed"`) and 279 (`_only_unavailable_gate(proj, "unavailable")`). These calls do not set `unit_tests` to the intended `unavailable`/`failed` state; they create or target a gate literally named `"unavailable"`/`"failed"`, so the new unit and end-to-end tests exercise a different project shape than their names claim, and the old windowed-rule test is altered to target the wrong gate.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_policy.py:230

chunk_findings.detail: The new predicate still over-fires because its final `return bool(names) and all(...)` only checks that the names in `target` have recorded outcomes `unavailable`/`partial`; it does not require those names to be required gates, nor that they are currently unsatisfied. The over-fire loop only rejects unmet required gates, so if every required gate is satisfied and `target` names a non-required (or otherwise satisfied) gate whose outcome happens to be unavailable/partial, the predicate returns True. For example, with `required_gates(cfg) == ("lint",)`, `pipeline_for(it, cfg) == ("lint", "docs")`, `lint` passed, `docs` recorded `unavailable`, and `target == "docs"`, the required-gate loop sees no unsatisfied required gate, then `names == ["docs"]` and `all(it.gate_outcome(g) in _UNAVAILABLE_OR_PARTIAL for g in names)` is true, so `complete_unavailable` auto-answers a `complete.force` ask even though no required gate is unmet, contrary to the intended “only unmet required gate is unavailable/partial” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:_unavailable_unmet_only

chunk_findings.detail: The diff fixes only cause (1): `_unavailable_unmet_only` now has a real predicate. It does not implement cause (2) from the stated intent: the routine `ddflow complete` path (no `--approval`) still must consult the standing rule. The new test confirms this gap by calling `C.operator_gate(...)` directly instead of exercising the real completion flow. Given the described input — a merged item whose only unmet required gate is `unit_tests=unavailable`, then running `ddflow complete` in the standing window — the predicate is now correct if invoked, but the nondiffed completion path still never invokes it, so the person-ask is still filed and `complete_unavailable` never auto-answers.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py

chunk_findings.detail: The routine completion path still only reaches the explicit-approval gate. `_auto_complete_unavailable` calls `_approved_force(..., approval="", ...)`, and `_approved_force` hard-codes `CN.operator_gate(..., approval_id=approval, auto=False)`; no code path sets `auto=True` or otherwise requests standing-rule application. Therefore, for a routine `ddflow complete` by an agent on an item whose verdict has one blocker and `v.unmet_gates == v.coverage_gates == ["unit_tests"]`, `_only_unavailable` returns true, but the call to `_approved_force` is still a no-approval explicit-approval check. It will not consume the standing `complete_unavailable` rule, returns not-ok, leaves `force` false, and the completion is refused—exactly the failure the change claims to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py:_auto_complete_unavailable/_approved_force

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate re-derives “unmet required gates” from `pipeline_for` plus `it.gate_satisfied`/`it.gate_outcome`, but the completion verdict’s unmet list is built by `_unsettled(..., excused, ..., state)` (see `ddflow/services/completion/rules.py`), which can settle required pipeline gates that are not reflected by a strict item outcome check. For example, if an item’s pipeline contains required gates `unit_tests` and `docs_check`, the actual diff excuses `docs_check` via `applies_when` (so `_unsettled` excludes it and `v.unmet_gates == ["unit_tests"]`) and `docs_check` has no recorded outcome, while `unit_tests` is unavailable, then with `target == "unit_tests"` the loop still visits `docs_check`, sees `gate_satisfied(...) == False` and an empty outcome, and returns `False`. The standing rule therefore refuses to auto-answer a completion whose only verdict-unmet required gate is unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:_unavailable_unmet_only

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate re-derives the item’s unmet gates from `pipeline_for` and `it.gate_satisfied(g, True)` instead of trusting the new `Verdict.unmet_gates` list produced by `_unsettled`. Unlike `_unsettled`, it has no `excused`/`state` visibility, so a required gate that was legitimately excused as not_applicable by `applies_when` is still inspected. For an item whose pipeline has `lint` (required, not_applicable/excused) and `unit_tests` (required, unavailable), `Verdict.unmet_gates` will be `["unit_tests"]`, but the loop will still see `lint`, whose outcome is `not_applicable`, and hit `return False` because it is not in `_UNAVAILABLE_OR_PARTIAL`. The completion site then still files `complete.force` with `target="unit_tests"`; `_unavailable_unmet_only` returns `False` even though the only verdict unmet gate is unavailable, so the rule still never fires for a common merged item with an excused gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:_unavailable_unmet_only

chunk_findings.detail: The end-to-end success test runs the final `complete` command with `agent="bot"` (and all commands in `_only_unavailable_repo` that wrote events used `agent="bot"`), but then it reads `EventLog(repo, "probe").read_all()`. `EventLog` is per-actor in ddflow — the same file uses `EventLog(proj, "bot")` as the log that `C.operator_gate` writes to — so the `"probe"` log is empty. The comprehension `[e for e in EventLog(repo, "probe").read_all() if e.kind == "item.completed"][-1]` produces `[]` and then `[-1]` raises `IndexError`. Thus this test fails regardless of whether the production fix is correct; it should read the `"bot"` event log.

data.text: Investigate the option to configure ddflow to lock files or directories individually only just before they are modified and how to unlock them potentially (offer merge from branch, cherry pick?) for others to work on the same files during the long waits for the gates and reviews to pass, and after the review to notify the others for the changes before the merge to the original branch on which they work (aka main). The goal is to break the long locks together with the new features of the DAG optimizer, the granular unit test runs, and merge of gates and reviews between work and agents. Check also the option to allow, if someone owns a file, others to work on it with an optimistic lock and send their small changes to the primary worker to integrate and pass on the gates. This way maybe we can break the blocking from the locking with minimal risk. Do a deep research on this as we are looking at how to speed up feature development.

data.body: Found 2026-11-02: release at enqueue hands an item to the merge queue, but the integrator (ddflow queue run) is run by 'any agent' and nothing triggers it (no daemon, ticks do not call it): a released item can wait with no lease and no owner. That is probably why the log has 0 lane.released_for_gate events. Add: (1) when a release is accepted, start one detached integrator run through the ddflow job machinery (single flight: a flock or job key so two never run, the queue already guarantees one integrator at a time), recorded as a job with its log path; (2) a tick fallback that starts the integrator when released or ready entries wait longer than [merge_queue].auto_run_after_s and no integrator job is alive; (3) brief, status and doctor say 'N released entries waiting, integrator not running: ddflow queue run' with the MCP form; (4) a parked entry wakes its lane (already designed) and the warning names it; (5) knobs [merge_queue].auto_run (on|off, default on), auto_run_after_s, auto_run_max_parallel (1); off still works by hand. Tests with a fake job starter and fake clock: release starts exactly one run, a second release while running starts none, a dead job is restarted by the tick, off starts nothing, warning text. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, D-sched-no-daemon, r-lock-cycle-selfheal): a knob, four ways to set it, org-lockable; every result names the exact next call in CLI and MCP form; no daemon. Operator 2026-11-02: turn on release-at-enqueue for this project and make it the ddflow default for all projects. Evidence: R-lock-inventory (leases are held a median 65 min; 45 percent of hold time is gates and reviews; lane.released_for_gate has fired 0 times).
data.title: Something must run the integrator: start it when an item is released, with a tick fallback and a visible warning when released entries wait with nobody integrating

data.body: Change the shipped default of [lanes].release_mode from flag to auto (choices off|flag|auto stay; strictest stays off for org policy). Eligibility is unchanged and is the safety: an item is released only when each judgement gate of release_gates is recorded passed on the current tree, so this frees the lease for the machine gates (ci, unit_tests, standards, merge) and does not yet cover the long review rounds (that is the follow-up lock-lifecycle phase). Update every place that asserts the default: knob manifest, constants ratchet, golden help/knob surface (tests/golden/** is a shared glob: regenerate through the pin recipe, do not hand-edit), docs, the agent-facing instructions that say 'you hold the lease until complete' (r-tell-dont-discover: after enqueue the agent is told the exact next call and that the lane is free), and an upgrade note in ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ so existing projects see the change and can pin flag with one command. This project already runs auto (set 2026-11-02 in its project config); keep that line as the explicit value. Tests: default is auto; an explicitly set flag or off wins; org lock to off holds; an item whose judgement gates are not passed is refused with the reason. Depends on LC-integrator-trigger so the default never strands an entry. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, D-sched-no-daemon, r-lock-cycle-selfheal): a knob, four ways to set it, org-lockable; every result names the exact next call in CLI and MCP form; no daemon. Operator 2026-11-02: turn on release-at-enqueue for this project and make it the ddflow default for all projects. Evidence: R-lock-inventory (leases are held a median 65 min; 45 percent of hold time is gates and reviews; lane.released_for_gate has fired 0 times).
data.title: Make [lanes].release_mode = auto the ddflow default for every project, with an upgrade note

data.body: Operator 2026-11-02: break the long locks together with the DAG optimizer, granular test runs and merged gates/reviews; lock files individually only just before modification and unlock them for others during the long gate and review waits; notify others of changes before the merge to main; let others work on an owned file optimistically and send their small changes to the owner who integrates and passes the gates; use git merges, cherry-picks, messages and notifications. Evidence: R-lock-inventory (hold time median 65 min, 45 percent in gates and reviews, 21 percent after the last commit, release-at-enqueue never used), R-lock-landscape and R-lock-landscape-verified (outside), R-handoff-protocol (experiments with cherry-pick, format-patch, hidden refs, bundle, merge-tree, patch-id). This phase MERGES the earlier unbuilt lock, wait, drift and sync tasks so all can run together: they were moved here from P-lane-consolidation, bugs-2, P-change-surface and the DX-* group. Supersedes the 'early release while only reviews run' rejection in D-lease-hold-limit-r2 (new decision filed with the phase).
data.title: Lock lifecycle: lock a file only when it is first written, release or downgrade during gates and reviews, notify others of merges and in-flight work, hand small changes to the owner, so long locks stop blocking parallel agents

data.alternatives: Only via the coordinator; no peer suggestions; owner may ignore and let the suggestion expire after a TTL (recommended default, not chosen)
data.context: Evidence R-handoff-protocol (git experiments: cherry-pick -x, format-patch + am -3, hidden refs, bundle, merge-tree probe 8 ms, patch-id/range-diff) and R-lock-inventory (median lease hold 65 min, 45 percent in gates and reviews). Consequence added by the coordinator for the owner-must-answer rule: the owner merge and complete refuse while any suggestion to it is unanswered; if the owner lease expires or is released with suggestions open, they are re-addressed to the next claimant or expire into ordinary tasks that need the owner item; a loop guard allows one open suggestion per sender-owner pair per file set.
data.decision: OPERATOR 2026-11-02: (1) AMENDS D-context-sync: besides the existing rules (operator may tell anyone; a master tells its children and peers on its items; an agent tells its master), an agent may send a SUGGESTION (a patch recorded as data, never an instruction or approval) to the agent that currently holds the lease on the file it needs. (2) Small only: up to 3 files and 60 lines by default ([handoff] knobs); bigger changes are ordinary tasks. (3) The owner must ALWAYS respond to every suggestion (accept and apply, or reject with a reason; counter allowed). (4) Once a suggestion is resolved (accepted or refuted) the suggester builds on that outcome and may send more, up to 5 open or sent per owner and file by default (configurable). (5) When the limit is reached the suggester waits until the file is released, or opens a new task for the remaining part and continues with the rest of its work when it can. (6) Auto-apply by the owner was NOT chosen: no automatic application, advice only; any later auto-apply needs a new decision.
data.title: An agent may send a bounded change suggestion to the lease holder of the file it needs; the owner must always answer it

data.alternatives: Log-only for a week then enforce (recommended, not chosen); keep claim-time globs and only narrow them; downgrade to a shared pending marker
data.context: R-lock-inventory, R-lock-landscape (ranked mechanisms 1-5), R-handoff-protocol. Safety kept by the coordinator: the write-time hook must be cheap (a cached lease snapshot; the measured full-log fold costs 3.7 s per call), and the project-level hook matcher currently covers Bash only so the hook installers must be extended for the write tools of each harness; harnesses without a blocking pre-tool hook fall back to the pre-commit check and say so (P-parity).
data.decision: OPERATOR 2026-11-02: (1) Lock-at-first-write is ENFORCED from the start (no log-only period): an Edit or Write on a file held by another agent is refused, the message names the holder and the exact options (wait, send a suggestion, open a task). It stays a knob ([locks] mode, org-lockable) so a project can set log-only or off. (2) EARLY RELEASE IS ALLOWED: a lease is held from the first write until the item is merge-ready, then released; if a review asks for edits the agent re-acquires per file and first rebases or syncs; a git merge-tree conflict probe at release and at merge, and ci on the merge result, stay mandatory. This reverses the rejected alternative 'early release of globs while only reviews run' in D-lease-hold-limit-r2 for the lock lifecycle only; the rest of D-lease-hold-limit-r2 (time-limited locks, break after hold_max_s) stands. (3) Reviews invalidated per file overlap: a rebase keeps a review when the item patch-id is unchanged and main changed none of the files the reviewers saw; otherwise only the overlapping files are re-reviewed.
data.title: Locks are taken at the first write, held to merge-ready and released; release at merge-ready with re-validation on re-edit

data.context: R-handoff-protocol stage 3. The owner-must-answer rule of D-handoff-peers still holds: the policy answer counts as the answer.
data.decision: OPERATOR 2026-11-02, answering the auto-apply question again: include auto-apply now, off by default. This narrows item 6 of D-handoff-peers (no auto-apply): ddflow may apply a suggestion on the owner behalf, recorded as accepted by policy, only when [handoff].auto_apply is switched on (default off, org-lockable) and ALL hold: 1 file and 10 lines or fewer (knobs), kind fix or doc, git merge-tree clean on the owner current tip, ci and the affected tests green on the merged result BEFORE the commit, commit keeps the contributor authorship with a Suggested-by trailer and the suggestion id. The owner is told afterwards in its next_actions with the exact revert call; the applied change is a new delta so its reviews are re-run for those files; a red result sends the suggestion to the owner as an ordinary one. Measured: accept rate, ci-red-after-apply, owner revert rate; a revert rate above a knob threshold switches auto-apply off with a visible note.
data.title: Owner auto-apply of tiny, probe-clean suggestions is built in the lock-lifecycle phase, OFF by default

data.body: Measured 2026-11-02 (R-lock-landscape-verified, 490 completed tasks): 33.5 percent of all lease-hours fall AFTER the merge; the median merge-to-release is 101 s but p90 is 8 h, because completion waits on approvals, the integrator, or an absent agent, while the item holds files nobody can change any more. Release the item leases in ddflow merge (and in the queue integrator) as soon as the merge lands and the event is recorded; complete then needs no lease. The hold of globs while only the completion steps remain is removed. Keep the worktree and branch for the completion steps. Tests: after merge the files are claimable by a waiter and a wake reason ready is sent; a failed merge keeps the lease; a merge via the queue releases too; complete still works without a lease (R3110c7c58b precedent). data.body: One small service and one declared command (ddflow probe ITEM [--against main|ITEM]) that runs git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only through infra.git, reads the exit code (0 clean, 1 conflicts; do NOT use --quiet: git 2.43 returns 129; the probe checks git version and falls back to a scratch merge when merge-tree is unusable), returns clean or the conflicting paths, and records the result as a probe event with the tip shas. Measured here: 8 to 21 ms typical, p90 1.3 s on 11k-commit-stale branches, 1.5 percent textual conflicts in 68 evaluable pairs. Honest limit written into the result text: clean means textually clean only; a semantic break (a renamed function used by the other side) still needs the gates and ci on the merge result. Used by: release at merge-ready, suggestion send, peer notices, review reuse. Knobs: [locks].probe (on), probe_timeout_s, probe_at (claim|gate|merge). data.body: Measured: the lane write check costs 3.7 s per call on this repository because it folds the 108 MB log. A per-edit hook cannot do that. Write a small snapshot (.ddflow/local/lease-snapshot.json: live leases with holder, globs, expiry; shared and new-file globs; the caller identity map) atomically on every lease acquire, renew, release and expire, with a generation counter, and let hooks read only it. A stale or missing snapshot makes the hook fail open to the commit-time check and say so (never a silent pass). Budget: hook under 30 ms p95, asserted by a test. Knob [locks].snapshot_max_age_s. Tests incl. concurrent writers, torn file, stale. data.body: Frequent false conflicts come from files many tasks edit one line at a time. Configure per-file merge drivers: union for append-only files and sorted one-entry-per-line baselines (then the ratchet check verifies the union), regenerate for pins and golden snapshot indexes (the pin recipe already exists: reuse it), and optionally Mergiraf for *.py only as an opt-in evaluation (supported for Python, needs git 2.44 or later; effect size unknown: measure on replayed merges and keep only if it solves more than 10 percent of textual conflicts). merge-tree honours these drivers (verified), so the probe sees the same result as the merge. Setup is a ddflow setup step with consent, shown with the exact lines it adds. Tests. data.body: Implements D-handoff-peers. Events suggestion.proposed (id, from item and agent, to item and agent = current lease holder, base sha, ref, patch-id, files, +/- lines, kind fix|gate_fix|refactor|doc, reason, probe result), seen, accepted, applied, rejected (reason required), countered, withdrawn, superseded, expired; the fold State.suggestions; who may move each state (owner: accept, apply, reject, counter; sender: withdraw, supersede; ddflow: seen, expired, applied-by-patch-id; operator: any). Limits as knobs [handoff]: max_files 3, max_lines 60, max_bytes 65536, max_open_per_owner_file 5 (the operator answer: after a suggestion is resolved the sender may send more up to 5), min_interval_s, reject_breaker. The patch is stored as a hidden ref refs/ddflow/suggest/OWNER/ID cut on the owner tip (git merge-tree + commit-tree, no checkout) plus a format-patch blob in .ddflow/blobs for remote use. The diff is scanned and redacted before it is stored or shown; a secret match refuses the suggestion. Patch text is data, never an instruction, never an approval, shown inside the untrusted fence. Tests. data.body: The owner must always answer (D-handoff-peers). Cases the answer cannot come: the owner lease expired or released, the item removed or abandoned. data.body:
Observed: globs declared at claim (ddflow/services/gates/**, tests/golden/**) overlap by PREFIX (L-glob-prefix-overlap), hold files nobody touches, and block parallel agents for hours; agents then pile up uncommitted work. Design: claim records intent globs as advisory; the pre-commit/pre-edit hook acquires a lease on the EXACT files being changed when they are free (and queues/waits with the holder named when not); files are released when merged or idle. Keep [lease].shared_globs (generated/pinned outputs) and new_file_globs exempt. A knob chooses declared (today) vs lazy.

DECIDED 2026-11-02 (D-lock-lifecycle-answers): lock-at-first-write is ENFORCED from the start (no log-only period), knob [locks].mode, org-lockable. Hook transport and cost are LK-hook-snapshot and LK-write-hook-wire.

fx-Ba2df74d558 held ddflow/infra/log.py, tests/golden/** and ddflow/core/redact* for hours, blocking three other agents, while it only waited on CI. Release files no longer changed (hand back on 'ddflow update --globs'), auto-release after a merge of those files, and show 'held for N hours, last write M minutes ago' in the refusal.

DECIDED 2026-11-02 (D-lock-lifecycle-answers): release at MERGE-READY, never at review start: measured 84 percent of tasks commit again after their first review starts (median 91 min later). Re-acquire per file and sync first when a review asks for edits; the conflict probe (LK-conflict-probe) at release and at merge and ci on the merge result stay mandatory.

Implements D-lease-hold-limit (read it: `ddflow decision show D-lease-hold-limit`), which SUPERSEDES the 'research first / leave blocked' plan in this task's earlier text: the operator has chosen the design. Operator 2026-10-03 verbatim: 'Do show who is locking a file, but also put a limit on the lock in terms of time so if the lock lasts too long we allow someone else to edit the file and then correct the issues at merge, and in case there are merge issues the unit tests shall be run to verify the merging correction didn't create own bugs and recessions. All of this behavior should be configurable, including timeout, unlocking, via config, cli or mcp.' Build: (a) config [lease].hold_max_s (default 3600, 0 = never), break_on_timeout (true), reconcile_tests (full|affected|off, default full), shipped defaults for ALL projects, settable in config.toml / local layer / env / `ddflow config` / MCP ddflow_configure. (b) claim logic (services/leases.py, services/waits.py, the claim-fairness registry B-fix-claim-fairness and the lease-contest machinery B-fix-contest-gaps): a claim overlapping a lease older than hold_max_s on contended globs is allowed and records lease.overlap; the holder is never evicted, keeps worktree/branch/lease; both briefs show the overlap; `ddflow lease break <item> --reason` (operator) and `ddflow lease keep <item> --for N` (holder may extend its own; operator any) and the MCP equivalents. (c) merge: when the merging item's files overlap another merged item since its base, or main-in merge conflicts, record merge.reconciled (files, base, main sha) and require a passing full unit suite (+ slow scenarios if on their path) on the reconciled tree before complete; evidence names files and run; --force --reason is the recorded exception. (d) fold/replay/doctor/brief/README/driver docs updated (D-readme-current). Acceptance (failing-first, deterministic fakes for time): a lease past hold_max_s with a waiter is breakable and a lease under it is not; a holder is never evicted; hold_max_s = 0 and break_on_timeout = false keep the old refusal; overlap is visible in both briefs; keep extends; two branches editing the same file merge with the second reconciled and complete REFUSED until the suite result is recorded; non-overlapping merges are not slowed; unlock and timeout settable via config --local and ddflow_configure; tools/list byte budget green; fold-order property tests green. Hot files (lifecycle.py, model.py, config.py, mcp.py): claim late, merge fast.

Phase B-hot-files; D-lease-hold-limit.

OPERATOR 2026-10-03: 'Make sure the latest is a general feature of ddflow, not only available to the work on this project.' => GENERALITY ACCEPTANCE (applies to this task): (1) the behaviour is code plus shipped defaults in the ddflow package, never a value or file that only this repository carries (no edit to this repo's .ddflow/config.toml or docs/ddflow as the way it is enabled; those may only be regenerated copies of shipped templates); (2) an EXISTING project upgrading ddflow, and a project created later by `ddflow init`/`adopt`, gets it with no config change (forward-compatible defaults; unknown-knob handling from older versions already notes, not breaks); (3) tests build a fresh throwaway project (tmp dir, `ddflow init`, no companions, no reviewer, no network) and prove it works there, and also work with the default-pipeline and a custom workflow; (4) no reference to this repository's paths, agent names, reviewers, hosts or models anywhere in code, messages or shipped docs; (5) documentation ships with the package: README and the shipped driver/prompt templates (ddflow/templates/**) describe it, so `ddflow init` / `ddflow prompts` / `ddflow help` surface it in any project; (6) it works for every agent integration (Claude Code, Gemini, Codex, Cursor, Kilo, opencode, plain CLI) because it lives in the core/CLI/MCP, not in one harness's hook.

RELATED 2026-11-02: the decisions and measurements are in D-lock-lifecycle-answers and R-lock-landscape-verified; LK-release-at-merge, LK-conflict-probe and DX-lease-release-early carry the build. Overlap by explicit break stays as D-lease-overlap-only-by-break says; suggestions (LK-sg-*) are the sanctioned way to touch a held file.

globs_overlap is prefix-based by design (L-glob-prefix-overlap, L-wildcard-globs-scheduler-overlap): 'a/**' overlaps 'a/x.py' though the holder never touches x.py. Compute overlap from the holder's actual changed files (git diff of its worktree against base plus its literal declared paths) so disjoint files under one directory run in parallel; fall back to the prefix rule only when the holder has no worktree.

RELATED 2026-11-01: OPT-signals uses the files a holder actually changed as the overlap signal; one predicate with core/admission.

MEASURED 2026-11-02: 32 percent of classifiable wait-hours (145 of 457) were between tasks whose real changed files were disjoint; LK-shared-readers and LK-optimizer-signals build on this task.

Change the shipped default of [lanes].release_mode from flag to auto (choices off|flag|auto stay; strictest stays off for org policy). Eligibility is unchanged and is the safety: an item is released only when each judgement gate of release_gates is recorded passed on the current tree, so this frees the lease for the machine gates (ci, unit_tests, standards, merge) and does not yet cover the long review rounds (that is the follow-up lock-lifecycle phase). Update every place that asserts the default: knob manifest, constants ratchet, golden help/knob surface (tests/golden/** is a shared glob: regenerate through the pin recipe, do not hand-edit), docs, the agent-facing instructions that say 'you hold the lease until complete' (r-tell-dont-discover: after enqueue the agent is told the exact next call and that the lane is free), and an upgrade note in ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ so existing projects see the change and can pin flag with one command. This project already runs auto (set 2026-11-02 in its project config); keep that line as the explicit value. Tests: default is auto; an explicitly set flag or off wins; org lock to off holds; an item whose judgement gates are not passed is refused with the reason. Depends on LC-integrator-trigger so the default never strands an entry. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, D-sched-no-daemon, r-lock-cycle-selfheal): a knob, four ways to set it, org-lockable; every result names the exact next call in CLI and MCP form; no daemon. Operator 2026-11-02: turn on release-at-enqueue for this project and make it the ddflow default for all projects. Evidence: R-lock-inventory (leases are held a median 65 min; 45 percent of hold time is gates and reviews; lane.released_for_gate has fired 0 times).

NOTE 2026-11-02: release at enqueue frees the lease only for machine gates after judgement gates passed. The lock lifecycle (this phase) covers the rest: release at merge (LK-release-at-merge) and at merge-ready.
